text:
Sam: hey folks, sam here, first day on runtime. trying to compile main on our lab workstation (ubuntu 22.04) with CUDA toolkit 12.0 installed side-by-side with 11.8. gcc 13. build fails at ptxas step with an odd message. any hints?
Sam: error log:
```
ptxas fatal : unsupported PTX version '9.0'
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda-12.0/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcudart_static.a(libcudart_static.a.o): relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Sam: building with `make -j8 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.0`
Jaya: welcome! first pass: mixed toolkits rarely play nice. PTX 9.0 implies toolkit 12+ emitted new PTX that your driver doesn't support. what does `nvidia-smi` report?
Sam: `nvidia-smi` -> Driver Version: 510.68.02 ; GPU: A100 and older GTX in the same machine
Eli: yep that's the mismatch. driver 510 won't understand PTX 9.0 from CUDA 12. Either upgrade driver to 525+ or force nvcc to generate older PTX. Also the relocation/fPIC error is because some static cudart object wasn't compiled position-independent while linking into a .so. building static objects into shared libs needs -fPIC.
Sam: can we do a quick workaround? can't bump drivers on this machine (it's shared infra).
Natanael: two practical workarounds: 1) build against CUDA 11.8 (remove /usr/local/cuda-12.0 from PATH/CUDA_HOME) so nvcc emits older PTX; or 2) add `-Xcompiler -fPIC` to NVCC flags and set `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` to target older SMs so PTX stays compatible. Example:
```
export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5;8.0"
export CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS="-Xcompiler -fPIC"
make BUILD_USE_CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-11.8 -j8
```
Jaya: also check `which nvcc` and `nvcc --version` to be sure the build picks the toolkit you expect. side-by-side installs confuse CI and local builds
Sam: `which nvcc` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.0/bin/nvcc ; `nvcc --version` -> release 12.0.221
Mika: since you can't change drivers, easiest is to pin to toolkit 11.8 for the build. We have a local build VM `buildbox-03` that infra maintains with drivers 525+. If you need to run GPU tests, use that. For pure build artifacts, switching to 11.8 should work.
Sam: how do i cleanly pick 11.8 when 12 is present?
Eli: prepend PATH and set CUDA_HOME before invoking make. e.g. `export PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin:$PATH; export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH; export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-11.8` then `make clean && make ...`
Sam: tried that but still saw `ptxas` from 12.0 during compile (weird).
Natanael: check `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version` too. sometimes nvcc wrapper still calls into /usr/local/cuda-12.0/bin/ptxas via hardcoded paths in build scripts. grep the build logs for `/usr/local/cuda-12.0` occurrences.
Sam: `which ptxas` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.0/bin/ptxas ; grepping build files found `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR` set in cmake cache pointing to 12.0. will update cache to 11.8 and retry.
Jaya: FYI for the fPIC problem, we added `-Xcompiler -fPIC` in our Makefile for shared lib builds a while ago; search for `CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS` in repo - there's a recommended flagset in `build/cuda.mk` you can import
Sam: updated cmake cache to 11.8, set NVCC flags to include fPIC, set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to 8.0, rebuild -> passes ptxas stage now but hits a runtime error when I try unit tests locally: `undefined symbol: cublasLtMatmul`
Eli: that symbol indicates the host driver lacks newer cublasLt API. That's expected with driver 510. For runtime tests you need a host with newer drivers (buildbox or CI). Locally you can mock cublas calls or run CPU-only tests.
Sam: ok makes sense. is there a documented developer flow for this case? where to find buildbox access and how to request driver upgrades?
Mika: yes, eng-runtime onboarding doc has a section. TL;DR: request buildbox access via the infra self-service ticket (link in handbook), or use the runtime-dev docker image if you only need consistent build env. Note: docker image still uses host driver for runtime.
infra-bot: Recommended dev image for builds: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc13-2026-03-10. For CI GPU runners see infra runbook: /internal/runbooks/runtime-gpu-runners.md (drivers 525+).
Sam: thanks. i'll: (1) switch local build to 11.8 and add fPIC flags; (2) push artifacts and run GPU tests on buildbox; (3) add a short note in onboarding docs about mixed-toolkit pitfalls.
Natanael: one more tip: if you patch cmake caches, run `git status` to ensure you don't accidentally commit local absolute paths. We prefer using environment overrides not committed files.
Sam: good call. will keep overrides in a local script `scripts/devsetenv.sh` and share gist here when done. thanks everyone!
Mika: welcome aboard Sam :wave: ping if you want pairing on first-week issues
Sam: appreciate it, will follow up with the gist and doc PR later.
